howToCalculate.title: How Brazilian CLT vacation is calculated
howToCalculate.p1: The calculation starts from base remuneration, formed by monthly salary plus habitual averages entered, and divides it by 30 to find the daily value.
howToCalculate.p2: The calculator multiplies the daily value by vacation days, adds the constitutional one-third and separates abono, deductions and manual adjustments.

constitutionalThird.title: What the constitutional one-third means
constitutionalThird.text: The one-third addition is added to vacation remuneration. This tool shows it separately so the receipt is easier to review.

abono.title: How abono pecuniario works
abono.p1: Abono can convert up to one-third of entitled vacation days into cash. With a 30-day entitlement, the common limit is selling 10 days and resting 20.
abono.p2: Ordinary salary for sold days is not a second vacation item; it is regular payroll for the worked days.

proportionalOverdue.title: Proportional, overdue and double vacation
proportionalOverdue.p1: In proportional mode, the tool counts months with at least 15 days in the acquisition period and applies the absence reduction.
proportionalOverdue.p2: In overdue mode, vacation start is compared with the concession-period deadline. Late payment alone does not create automatic double pay in this estimate.

deductions.title: Which deductions may appear on vacation
deductions.p1: For normal vacation, the estimate calculates INSS and IRRF with 2026 tables on rested vacation plus one-third, excluding abono from automatic bases.
deductions.p2: Payroll can combine bases, advances and ceilings differently, so manual deduction and addition fields are available.

payrollDifference.title: Why the receipt may differ from payroll
payrollDifference.text: Variable averages, collective agreements, advances, payroll competence, INSS ceiling already used and eSocial setup can change the official net value.

disclaimer.title: Important notice
disclaimer.text: This calculator provides an educational estimate, not legal, tax, accounting or payroll advice. Official payroll, eSocial, collective agreements and professional review prevail.

q1.question: How do I calculate vacation with one-third?
q1.answer: Divide remuneration by 30, multiply by vacation days and add one-third of that value. The calculator separates each line in the memo.

q2.question: How much more do I receive by selling 10 days?
q2.answer: Abono adds the sold-day value and its one-third to the vacation receipt. Ordinary salary for worked days is shown separately to avoid double counting.

q3.question: Does abono pecuniario pay INSS or IRRF?
q3.answer: In this estimate, abono and one-third on abono are outside automatic INSS and IRRF bases according to the sources checked. Official payroll should still be reviewed.

q4.question: Are overdue vacations always paid double?
q4.answer: Double pay appears when the concession period is missed. Partial or disputed cases should be reviewed by payroll, union, accountant or lawyer.

q5.question: Does late payment automatically create double pay?
q5.answer: Not in this estimate. The tool does not apply double pay only because payment occurred after the two-day-before-vacation deadline.

q6.question: Do unjustified absences reduce vacation?
q6.answer: Yes. The calculator uses the 30, 24, 18, 12 or 0 day brackets based on unjustified absences in the acquisition period.

q7.question: Is proportional vacation the same as severance?
q7.answer: Not necessarily. This mode estimates acquisition-period avos; severance can have its own rules, deductions and additional items.

q8.question: Does the calculator show the exact net value?
q8.answer: No. It estimates from entered data and 2026 tables. Official payroll can change because of averages, advances, INSS ceiling, agreements and eSocial setup.
